summary: The exact candidate adds a meaningful eager ordinary-decode cascade path and passes its portable regression, but it is not a full integration of the original feature request. CUDA-graph replay and multiple supported attention/KV modes intentionally retain ordinary decode, while the only real FlashInfer wrapper and merge-kernel regression skipped on the prepared ROCm host. The candidate is therefore a partial fix with useful test hardening, not a verified complete fix.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before execution of the candidate regression against the recorded base; cascade helpers, metadata, updater, and forward behavior are absent.
Candidate regression: 6 passed, 1 skipped, 7 subtests passed. The real FlashInfer wrapper/merge integration was the skipped test.
Independent GPU checks for prefix mismatch, threshold boundaries, zero-suffix planning shape, and source-confirmed exclusions for graph/speculative/dispatch/dequant paths.
Changed Python source and regression test compile.
Exact candidate has no whitespace errors relative to the recorded base.

gpu_execution_evidence: One AMD Instinct MI350X executed the portable float64 split-softmax regression and independent adversarial tensor checks under Torch 2.11.0+rocm7.2. No FlashInfer kernel executed because torch.version.cuda is null and FlashInfer is unavailable.
remaining_counterexamples: CUDA-graph decode always uses the existing ordinary decode wrappers; shared-prefix cascade is not integrated into graph replay.
Sliding-window attention, encoder-decoder cross attention, speculative decode, and dequant-workspace KV cache configurations explicitly do not use cascade.
Actual BatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheWrapper forward_return_lse and production merge_state kernel execution remains unverified because the gated integration test skipped.
No NVIDIA serving benchmark or end-to-end shared-prefix request workload verifies serving correctness or the intended latency/throughput benefit.
remaining_limitations: Prepared hardware is AMD ROCm, while FlashInfer cascade execution requires NVIDIA CUDA in this test suite.
FlashInfer is not installed/available in the pinned interpreter, so wrapper planning, cache layout, numerical kernel correctness, and kernel compatibility could not be qualified.
No native source changed; native rebuild was not applicable.
The qualified tiny Llama fixture validates transport and engine execution only and cannot exercise or qualify the unavailable FlashInfer CUDA path.
